content:
Ravi Menon: need to lock down streaming shadowing semantics today-ish. edge cases are getting spicy.

Ravi Menon: questions:
1) if control request is `stream=true`, do we also stream to shadow target or force `stream=false`?
2) what do we store if shadow stream times out mid-way?
3) do we score partial outputs or drop them?

Vikram Singh: +1. data plane POV: mirroring a streaming request 1:1 means we’re keeping an extra connection open per sampled req. doable but increases fd/concurrency pressure. forcing `stream=false` on shadow reduces that but changes behavior for some models (esp stop reasons, tool calls etc).

Mina Haddad: routing wants deterministic apples-to-apples. but also we cannot let shadow add tail latency or soak connections. can we do: control stays streaming, shadow is non-streaming with a hard timeout + max_tokens cap?

Benji Okafor: control plane policy can allow either. but we need a default. i’d prefer default shadow uses `stream=false` even if control streamed.

Ravi Menon: if we flip stream flag on shadow, do we need to also adjust `max_tokens`? otherwise a long-running generation blocks worker resources.

Vikram Singh: yes. propose shadow request uses:
- `stream=false`
- `max_tokens = min(control_max_tokens, policy.shadow_max_tokens)`
- `timeout_ms = policy.shadow_timeout_ms` (strict)
- `top_p/temp/etc` same as control (unless variant overrides)

Mina Haddad: what about cases where control uses client disconnect? user closes SSE early -> control cancels. do we cancel shadow too?

Vikram Singh: i’d say no, shadow continues until its own timeout/cap. otherwise we get biased samples (lots of cancellations on long responses).

Sean Gallagher: SRE take: shadow should be fully decoupled from client lifecycle. treat shadow as best-effort background work. if shadow path is overloaded, circuit-break + drop. but do not hook it to client disconnect.

Allison Grant: observability side: we need to label outcomes. at minimum: `shadow_outcome = ok | timeout | error | dropped | truncated`. plus `shadow_duration_ms` and token counts. partial vs full matters for metrics.

Logan Wright: on ingestion: partial chunks are a cardinality + storage risk if we store raw chunk stream. pls don’t.

Ravi Menon: agreed, we shouldn’t store per-chunk events. question is whether we store the partial generated text if it times out.

Logan Wright: storing partial full text is also risky; but we already have redaction/truncation pipeline. could store *final assembled text* up to `max_chars` and a flag `is_partial=true`. no chunk-level.

Chloe Martin: Console UX will need to explain partials. if we include partials in scoring, users will see regressions that are just timeouts. i vote: by default don’t include partial outputs in “quality delta” aggregates.

Mina Haddad: +1. we can still chart shadow timeouts as reliability/overhead metric but don’t mix with “answer correctness”.

Ravi Menon: ok so scoring pipeline behavior:
- if shadow times out and we have partial text, we store it for debug/examples (redacted/truncated)
- mark `score_status=skipped_timeout`
- exclude from quality aggregates by default
sound right?

Allison Grant: yes, but we should include in denominator somewhere. two views:
1) Quality metrics on “scored set”
2) Coverage metrics: `scored_rate`, `timeout_rate`, `dropped_rate`
otherwise teams can “win” by timing out.

Sean Gallagher: 100%. also need guardrail alerts on coverage dropping.

Vikram Singh: implementation detail: even if we force `stream=false` on shadow, underlying inference engine can still internally stream tokens. but the network response is single payload. we can set a server-side deadline.

Ravi Menon: tool/function calling: some clients stream tool call deltas. if shadow is non-streaming, do we still capture tool calls? (structured output)

Vikram Singh: should. the final response object includes tool calls / structured fields. we’d capture the same response schema.

Mina Haddad: but if control is streaming and uses “early tool call” behavior (model emits tool call quickly), the client may act on it. shadow not affecting user anyway. so ok.

Benji Okafor: policy fields to add:
- `shadow_stream_mode: inherit | force_off` (default force_off)
- `shadow_timeout_ms` default 2000? (needs perf data)
- `shadow_max_tokens` default 256?
- `store_partial_shadow_response: true/false` (default true but redacted/truncated)
- `score_partials: true/false` (default false)

Ravi Menon: timeout defaults: 2s might be too aggressive for long-context. but we can separate:
- `shadow_connect_timeout_ms`
- `shadow_deadline_ms` total

Sean Gallagher: please keep it simple v1. one `shadow_deadline_ms` is fine. SRE will push for hard cap and a circuit breaker.

Logan Wright: also note scoring lag: if we include partial responses, scoring templates may fail (format adherence etc). skipping is safer.

Chloe Martin: UI: can show a banner “X% of shadow requests weren’t scored (timeouts/drops). Quality deltas computed over remaining N samples.”

Allison Grant: + include tooltip that low scored_rate widens confidence intervals.

Mina Haddad: another edge case: streaming control can run indefinitely if client is slow to read (backpressure). but that’s client-side. shadow should not inherit that. forcing non-streaming helps.

Vikram Singh: good point. also for streaming shadow=on, we’d need to implement chunk forwarding + buffer management. i’d rather not.

Ravi Menon: so decision seems: shadow request is non-streaming by default regardless of control. store assembled response (truncated) when available; if deadline hits, store partial + mark timeout; do not score partials.

Benji Okafor: works. we’ll document as “streaming shadowing semantics v1”. and add a note that in future we may support `inherit` for parity.

Sean Gallagher: one more: when shadow target is degraded, do we stop reading control stream? (NO) just drop shadow. data plane must be fail-open.

Vikram Singh: yup. shadow path in separate async task. no awaits on control path.

Ravi Menon: action items:
- Vikram: update routing spec w/ `force_off` default + deadline behavior
- Benji: add policy fields + validation (shadow_timeout in [250ms, 10s]?)
- Logan/Allison: outcome/coverage metrics proposal
- Chloe: UI copy for partial/timeouts + denominator explanation

Mina Haddad: :thumbsup:

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: I’ll draft the outcome enum + dashboards breakdowns.

Logan Wright: :+1: will sanity check storage impact w/ “store partial” on.

Chloe Martin: ack. will add to UX spec as “Scoring coverage” section.

Ravi Menon: cool. i’ll summarize in ADR comments and link this thread.
